From: Redwood Security & Compliance

Subject: Re: Questions re: log/backups retention and deletion for DPA compliance

Hi Jane — thanks for the detailed list. Below is a short mapping of Redwood's operational retention for the items you called out. If you'd like us to produce a formal attestation we can schedule a Soc2 evidence package delivery.

1) Application request logs (metadata only)
- Retention: default 90 days in hot storage for operational observability. After 90 days logs are automatically expired from primary storage.
- Backups: nightly incremental backups retained for 90 days. Backups are not immutable; they are subject to deletion schedules and may exist in backup windows until expiration. We do not restore user-level backups for ad-hoc deletion — see note on erasure below.

2) Backups (full/incremental)
- Frequency: incremental nightly; full snapshots weekly for cluster images.
- Retention windows: incremental 90 days; full snapshots 365 days for disaster recovery.
- Deletion model: backups are lifecycle-managed; they are not write-once immutable by default, but retention policies prevent accidental deletion.

3) Prompt/input data (hosted inference)
- Retention: by default we do not persist customer-provided prompts beyond the inference transaction in hot model-serving caches. Telemetry/metadata used for billing and debugging (request size, error codes) is retained up to 90 days.
- Optional: customers can opt-in to logging for fine-grained quality or evaluation; when enabled, those logs are retained per the customer's configured retention profile (we maintain a maximum cap of 730 days).

4) GDPR Right to Erasure
- Process: upon a verified erasure request, we delete customer-identifying artifacts from primary stores within 30 days.
- Backups: deletion from backups occurs as part of normal backup expiration; we cannot guarantee immediate removal from existing encrypted snapshots. In practice, data will be removed from active stores within 30 days and from backups within the backup retention window (see above).

Notes/controls: attached is a matrix showing the mapping to SOC2 CC6/CC7 controls and our DPA clauses.

Would you like us to (a) reduce primary log retention to 30 days for Acme under contract, or (b) document a policy exception to keep 365-day full snapshots for a specified compliance purpose?

Regards,
Redwood Security & Compliance
-----End Draft-----

Attachments: redwood_data_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx; SOC2-Incident-Controls-Overview.pdf

Please flag anything inaccurate. Rishi — could you confirm whether the weekly full snapshots are kept on immutable WORM storage for any customers (I believe not, but want to confirm).

Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Operations, Redwood Inference

Laura / team — technical confirmations below:

- Nightly incremental backups are stored in encrypted object storage with lifecycle rules; they are not WORM by default. We can enable a WORM/immutability policy for specific buckets on a per-customer basis, but that changes our restore/deletion semantics and requires a contract amendment.
- Weekly full snapshots are retained for 365 days in the DR retention tier; these snapshots are not included in standard erasure runs and will expire as per retention policy.
- We do not write prompt text into long-term logs by default. Prompt text is processed in-memory and cached briefly for model KV cache. If a customer opts into logging for ops/debugging we route that to a separate log stream with a configurable retention TTL.

If Acme asks for logs to be excluded from backups for erasure purposes, we would need to evaluate which artifact types to exclude and implement an exclusion policy. That is possible, but will require a short SRE rollout (1–2 weeks) and a contractual addendum.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
